summary: 小班能否提高成绩，取决于怎样比较班级、学校怎样实施。文章对照田纳西的随机实验、加州的大规模推行和威斯康星的定向试点。
logic: 加州和 SAGE 的经验

paragraphs.brief: 缩小班级规模为何受欢迎
sentences: Of all the ideas for improving education, few are as simple or attractive as reducing the number of pupils per teacher.
在改进教育的所有想法中，很少有像减少每名教师的学生人数这样简单或有吸引力。
Unlike competing proposals for reform, class-size reductions rarely elicit huge outcries or involve structural change.
与其他教育改革方案相比，缩小班额很少激起强烈反对，也不要求结构性调整。
The testing of educators, by contrast, generally arouses the anger of unions.
相比之下，对教育工作者的测试通常会引起工会的愤怒。
Similarly, establishing special ‘charter’ schools involves privileging some schools over others, with the credits provided usually coming out of the budgets of struggling local schools.
同样，设立特殊的「特许学校」意味着让部分学校享受优待，而拨给它们的经费通常从本已困难的当地学校预算中划出。

With its uncomplicated appeal, class-size reduction in the U.S. has lately gone from being a subject of primary academic interest to a policy juggernaut with over twenty states aiming at decreasing class sizes.
缩小班额的主张简单而有吸引力，在美国已从主要由学界讨论的议题变成势头强劲的政策，二十多个州都希望降低班级人数。
paragraphs.gist: 与考核教师或设立特许学校相比，缩小班级规模较少引起反对，也不要求大幅改造制度，因而迅速成为美国多州的政策。

paragraphs.brief: 旧数据中的辍学率与比较偏差
sentences: Do small classes improve school achievement?
小班能提高学校成绩吗？
To answer this, investigators have attempted to analyse existing data, such as records at the U.S. Department of Education.
为了回答这个问题，调查人员试图分析现有数据，例如美国教育部的记录。
These reveal that there were steep drops in pupil-teacher ratios between 1969 and 1997, but no significant gains in academic performance.
这些结果表明，1969年至1997年期间，学生与教师的比率急剧下降，但学业成绩没有显著提高。
But do these findings mean that class size makes no difference?
但这些结果能说明班级人数多少毫无影响吗？
Not necessarily.
不一定。
For instance, schools strive for more than just high test scores; they also usually try to keep their drop-out rates low.
例如，学校争取的不仅仅是高考试分数；它们通常还试图保持低辍学率。
And, indeed, the drop-out rate for older students fell considerably over that period.
事实上，在这一期间，年龄较大的学生的辍学率大幅下降。
Because drop-outs generally come from the low end of the achievement distribution, a reduction in the drop-out rate could be expected to pull down average test scores.
由于辍学者往往是成绩偏低的学生，辍学率下降、这些学生继续参加考试，就可能拉低平均成绩。
Another reason for discounting those data is the difficulty of ensuring a level playing field.
这些数据不宜被看得太重还有另一个原因：很难确保比较双方处于相同条件。
In a perfect world, U.S. students would all come from well-off families, with two highly educated English-speaking parents who are involved in their children’s schooling.
在一个完美的世界里，美国学生都来自富裕家庭，有两个受过高等教育的英语家长参与其子女的学校教育。
Teachers would all be creative and have complete mastery of the subject matter.
教师都具有创造性，完全掌握了课程内容。
The reality is very different.
现实大不一样。
paragraphs.gist: 美国师生比下降而平均分未显著上升，不能就此判定小班无用，因为更多低分学生留校、家庭条件和师资差异都会影响比较。

paragraphs.brief: 田纳西州随机分班试验
sentences: Over the past 35 years, some studies of existing data have produced evidence that smaller classes benefit students, but most of these studies were poorly designed.
在过去35年中，对现有数据的一些研究证明，小班对学生有利，但大多数这类研究设计不当。
The exception was the Tennessee study called Project STAR (Student Teacher Achievement Ratio).
例外是田纳西州的「学生教师成绩比率」研究，即 STAR 项目。
Frederick Mosteller of Harvard University has called it ‘one of the greatest experiments in education in United States history’.
哈佛大学的Frederick Mosteller称其为“美国历史上教育领域最伟大的实验之一”。

Students entering kindergarten were randomly assigned to one of three kinds of classes: a small class of 13 to 17 students, a regular-size class of 22 to 26 or a regular-size class with both a teacher and a full-time teacher’s aide.
幼儿园新生被随机分入三类班级：13至17人的小班、22至26人的普通班，或在教师以外再配备一名全职助教的普通班。
The students remained in whatever category they had been assigned to throughout the third grade, after which they joined a regular classroom in the fourth.
学生从幼儿园到三年级结束一直留在原先分配的班型，四年级才统一进入普通班。
To ensure that teaching quality did not differ, teachers were randomly assigned to small and regular-size classrooms.
为避免师资差异，教师也被随机分派到小班或普通班。
Few teachers received any special training for working with small classes, and there were no new curricular materials.
很少有教师接受过与小型班级合作的任何特殊培训，也没有新的教材。
paragraphs.gist: 田纳西州 STAR 试验将新生随机分入小班、普通班或配助教的普通班，教师也随机分配，让研究者能较公平地比较学习成果。

paragraphs.brief: 小班成效及对持久性的质疑
sentences: At the end of STAR, researchers analysed the data.
在STAR结束时，研究人员分析了数据。
Jeremy Finn of New York University and Charles Achilles of Eastern Michigan University found evidence for ‘an array of benefits of small classes’.
纽约大学的Jeremy Finn 和密歇根东部大学的Charles Achilles 都找到了`小班的一系列好处'的证据。

They calculated that students in smaller classes were outperforming their counterparts in regular-sized classes by the first grade and that this advantage persisted even after students returned to larger classes.
他们算出，到一年级时小班学生已超过普通班同龄人，而且即使回到较大的班级，优势仍然存在。
They also found that the effect was stronger for black and Hispanic minority groups – a significant finding for policy-makers.
他们也发现，对黑人和西班牙裔少数群体的影响更大，这是决策者的重要发现。
Eric Hanushek of Stanford, however, criticises some of STAR’s key conclusions.
但斯坦福的Eric Hanushek批评STAR的一些关键结论。
He argues that STAR does not prove that gains persist long after students return to regular classes.
他认为，STAR没有证明学生重返普通班很久以后，优势仍会持续。
It was debatable how much later improvement stemmed from other factors, such as a supportive home.
后来取得的进步有多少来自有支持的家庭环境等其他因素，仍有争议。
Nor does he accept that the benefits accumulate, with participants widening the gap with their peers in larger classes year by year.
他也不接受优势会逐年累积、使参与者与大班同龄人的差距不断拉大的说法。
Hanushek and others have also shown that during the study too many children moved from regular to small classes, probably because school personnel caved in to parent demands.
哈努谢克等人还指出，研究期间从普通班转入小班的儿童过多，很可能是学校人员向家长的要求让了步。
And Hanushek also asserts that STAR failed to ensure good randomisation of teacher and student assignments.
哈努谢克还认为，STAR并未确保分配教师和学生时做到充分随机。
However, these points do not undermine STAR’s basic findings.
然而，这些要点并不破坏STAR的基本调查结果。
paragraphs.gist: STAR 发现小班优势在一年级就出现，对部分少数族裔尤其明显；批评者则质疑长期效果，以及家长要求调班对随机分组的干扰。

paragraphs.brief: 加州减班额加剧师资差距
sentences: The largest public class size reduction programme so far, California’s, stands more as a warning than as worthy of emulation.
迄今规模最大的公立学校缩小班额计划在加州，其经验更值得引以为戒。
That state is trying to reduce classes in kindergarten through grade three despite a shortage of teachers that is most acute in low-income areas.
该州试图缩减幼儿园至三年级的班额，然而师资本已短缺，在低收入地区尤其严重。
This is exacerbating the disparity in resources available to rich and poor schools in California, because more affluent areas can attract the best teachers.
这加剧了加利福尼亚富人和穷人学校在资源方面的差异，因为较富裕地区可以吸引最好的教师。
Indeed, some of the extra teachers needed are being recruited from the poorer schools.
实际上，需要的一些额外教师是从较贫穷的学校招聘的。
Researchers found a statistically significant achievement advantage in reading, writing and mathematics for students in classes that had been reduced to 20.
研究者发现，班额降到二十人的学生在阅读、写作和数学方面均有统计显著的成绩优势。
What is more, the effect did not vary for students of different backgrounds.
而且学生背景不同，这一效果并未随之改变。
paragraphs.gist: 加州把班额压到二十人后读写算成绩有所提高，但师资短缺使富裕地区从贫困学校吸走教师，反而扩大了校际资源差距。

paragraphs.brief: 威州针对贫困学校开展试点
sentences: Wisconsin’s Student Achievement Guarantee in Education (SAGE) was a five-year pilot study to do some of the groundwork for a major project.
威斯康星州学生教育成就保障(SAGE)是一项为期五年的试点研究，为一个重大项目打下基础。
Class sizes were reduced in only 14 schools, but it was noteworthy for targeting schools at which 30% of the students were below poverty level, compared with California’s across-the-board approach.
试点只在十四所学校缩小班额，其特色是针对贫困线以下学生占三成的学校，与加州全面推行的做法不同。
SAGE lowered the average pupil-teacher ratio in kindergarten through third grade to 12–15:1 from 21–25:1.
SAGE把幼儿园至三年级平均每位教师负责的学生人数从21至25人降至12至15人。
Analysts have studied the results of first-grade students in these schools and similar first-grade students elsewhere and found the results accord with those from STAR.
分析员研究了这些学校一年级学生和其他地方类似一年级学生的结果，发现其结果与STAR的结果一致。
STAR and SAGE have made it hard to argue against reducing class sizes.
有了STAR和SAGE的结果，就很难再反对缩小班额。
But the California initiative shows that reductions made with too little forethought can yield minuscule gains.
但加州的做法也说明，若事前考虑不足，缩小班额所获收益可能微乎其微。
Administrators need solid information before they can make sensible policy decisions.
教育管理者需要可靠信息，才能作出合理的政策决定。
paragraphs.gist: 威斯康星州集中在贫困生较多的十四所学校试行小班，结果支持 STAR；相比加州全面推行的经验，针对性和事前规划尤为重要。

items.en: detailed criticism of the methodology of a project
items.zh: 对某个项目研究方法的具体批评
items.why: D 段集中列出哈努谢克对 STAR 研究方法的质疑，包括教师和学生分配到各班的过程是否充分随机。

items.en: a comparison of the data from class-size reduction projects
items.zh: 比较几个缩小班额项目的数据
items.why: F 段比较 SAGE 学校一年级学生与其他地区类似学生的结果，又指出结论与 STAR 项目相符，因此涉及不同小班项目的数据对照。

items.en: the level of public interest in the issues of class-size reduction
items.zh: 公众对缩小班额有多关心
items.why: 小班教学从主要限于学术界的议题发展为二十多个州推进的政策，A 段用这一变化体现公众和政策界的关注程度。

items.en: details of action taken to protect the validity of a project
items.zh: 研究人员采取了哪些措施来保证项目结论可信
items.why: C 段说明研究者把教师随机分到小班和普通班，以避免把教学质量差异误当成班级规模的效果，这是保障研究有效性的措施。

items.en: reasons why class composition changed during a project
items.zh: 项目实施过程中，班级学生构成发生变化的原因
items.why: 有些家长要求子女转入小班，校方可能在压力下同意，从而使试验中的学生从普通班转走。D 段解释的是班级构成变化的原因。

items.en: The student composition of each class was left to chance.
items.zh: 各班学生都是随机分配的。

items.en: A long-term improvement in performance was claimed.
items.zh: 有研究者称，学生的学业表现得到了长期改善。

items.en: Similar results were obtained for all social groups.
items.zh: 所有社会群体都取得了类似成果。

items.en: The project was a preliminary to a more comprehensive study.
items.zh: 这项先导项目为规模更大的研究作准备。

items.en: Several different class types were involved in the project.
items.zh: 这项研究涉及数种不同类型的班级。

items.en: A special group of schools was selected to take part.
items.zh: 研究者专门挑选了一批学校参加项目。

items.en: Classroom assistants were used as part of the project.
items.zh: 项目在课堂上配备了助教。

items.en: The project was responsible for aggravating existing problems.
items.zh: 该项目加重了现有的问题。

items.en: Certain groups of pupils within the sample were identified as having benefited.
items.zh: 研究发现，样本中某些群体的学生从项目中获益。

pairs: 题目说班里的学生由机遇决定，原文说明具体做法是随机分班。
Similar results were obtained for all social groups
the effect did not vary for students of different backgrounds
题目说各群体结果相近，原文用否定句说明效果不随学生背景而变。
points: D 段集中列出哈努谢克对 STAR 研究方法的质疑，包括教师和学生分配到各班的过程是否充分随机。
题干问“有人声称，履约情况有长期改善”。定位句写到“他们计算出，在一年级以前，小班学生在正规班级的表现优于同班学生，即使在学生返回大班级后，这一优势仍然存在”。
clauses: These reveal …, but no significant gains in academic performance.
“that there were steep drops in pupil-teacher ratios between 1969 and 1997”补足 reveal 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 reveal 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
…, a reduction in the drop-out rate could be expected to pull down average test scores.
连接词 because 引出“Because drop-outs generally come from the low end of the achievement distribution”，说明主句的原因关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 because 把这一层关系补进去。
